turns.en: Welcome to Swimming with Alligators. The VC podcast from the LP perspective. With your host, Alexa Bins. And Ernest, you ready? Let's dive in. Welcome to the show. Today, we have Thomas Knowles, managing partner and co-CEO of Gratitude Ventures. This includes a network of 150 family offices,
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Swimming with Allocators——一档站在 LP 视角看 VC 的播客。我是主持人 Alexa Binns。Earnest，你准备好了吗？我们下水吧。欢迎来到节目。今天我们请到了 Gratitude Ventures 的管理合伙人兼联席 CEO Thomas Knowles。这家公司背后是一个由 150 家家族办公室（family office）组成的网络，

turns.en: all working with him as a community of investors focused on mission-driven businesses. He's the investment manager, working on behalf of all of these families. Thomas, we're so eager to hear your perspective. Thank you. By traveling. You didn't start at Gratitude Ventures. This is the latest iteration of your life.
turns.zh: 他们作为一个投资者社群与他并肩作战，聚焦使命驱动型（mission-driven）企业。他是替所有这些家族打理资金的投资管理人。Thomas，我们太期待听到你的看法了。谢谢你专程过来。你并不是从 Gratitude Ventures 起步的，这只是你人生最新的一次迭代。

turns.en: Can you walk us through your LP journey and your direct investing journey? Sure, absolutely. The connection to Gratitude started in undergraduate. I studied economics and got exposed to microfinance when it was really becoming a mainstream tool in the mid-2000s. And thought it was such an impressive way
turns.zh: 能不能带我们走一遍你的 LP 之路和直接投资之路？当然可以。我和 Gratitude 的缘分从本科就开始了。我学的是经济学，2000 年代中期正好接触到小额信贷（microfinance），当时它正在真正变成一种主流工具。我觉得这是一种非常了不起的方式，

turns.en: to use the capital markets to drive social mobility. But at that time, it was really done in the nonprofit sector and coming out of school, I wanted to go earn some high income and then maybe come back to impact down the road. And so started my career actually in the asset management arm of Silicon Valley Bank SUV capital.
turns.zh: 用资本市场去推动社会流动。但那时候这事基本只在非营利部门里做，而刚毕业的我，想先去挣一份高收入，也许日后再回到影响力这条路上。所以我职业生涯的起点，其实是在 Silicon Valley Bank 的资产管理板块 SVB Capital。

turns.en: I got the experience of being there through the financial crisis in 2007, 2008. And at the time when I joined, we had about a dozen investment professionals grew to multiples of that. And then back down to a small team. So just that experience continues to be part of my career today. And then when got some operating experience,
turns.zh: 我在那里完整经历了 2007、2008 年的金融危机。我加入时，投资团队只有十来个人，后来扩张到好几倍，然后又缩回一个小团队。这段经历至今仍然是我职业生涯的一部分。之后我也去积累了一些运营经验，

turns.en: so work for two technology companies doing corporate development. So acquisitions and investments. And then decided I wanted to get back to investing and really thought about what I wanted to do and how I wanted to invest in that experience of microfinance and having purpose and impact crept up
turns.zh: 在两家科技公司做企业发展（corporate development），也就是并购和投资。后来我决定回到投资行业，认真想了想自己要做什么、想怎么投，而当年做小额信贷、追求目标与影响力（impact）的那段经历又浮了上来，

turns.en: and found that our other co-founders at graduate ventures and started the organization in 2015. We've gotten feedback from a lot of our listeners that the historical context is always extremely helpful. And so I would be curious to get your perspective from what SBB Capital was doing to where you have come to now.
turns.zh: 于是我找到了 Gratitude Ventures 的另外几位联合创始人，在 2015 年把这家机构办了起来。说到这儿——我们收到过很多听众反馈，说历史背景总是特别有帮助。所以我很想听听你的视角：从 SVB Capital 当年做的事，到你今天走到的这一步。

turns.en: Are there any sort of like thematic shifts or like mental approaches to a mission and investing that you've seen that you can kind of like catch our folks up on who maybe weren't living it the way you were? Yeah, absolutely. I think one on the more philosophical side is part of my experience during that time
turns.zh: 有没有一些主题上的变化，或者对待使命与投资的心态上的变化，是你亲眼见过、可以帮那些没像你一样身在其中的人补一下课的？有，当然有。我觉得比较偏理念层面的一点是，那段时间我的切身感受是，

turns.en: was feeling that venture and entrepreneurship were not being used in terms of kind of the highest value ways. It was relatively short term oriented for an asset class that's supposed to be the longest term focused asset class and entrepreneurs that were focused on solutions that really addressing key social and environmental problems.
turns.zh: 风险投资和创业这两种力量，并没有被用在价值最高的地方。对一个本该是最长期的资产类别来说，它反而相当短视；而那些本应聚焦于解决关键社会与环境问题的创业者，

turns.en: It was more how can I sell this business to Salesforce in three years as an example I give. So I think philosophically I was just feeling like gosh, there's an opportunity to think about using this really finite resource of venture capital and entrepreneurship to address more important societal problems.
turns.zh: 想的更多是“我怎么能三年就把这家公司卖给 Salesforce”——这是我常举的例子。所以在理念上我当时就在想：天哪，这里明明有个机会，可以把风险投资和创业这种极其有限的资源，用来解决更重要的社会问题。

turns.en: And then, yeah, I think from a business model perspective as we'll get into in terms of our investment management organization at graduate ventures, a lot of similarities. So we have a fund of funds business. We do direct investing. We also do our active in the secondary's market.
turns.zh: 另外，从商业模式的角度看——后面我们会讲到我们在 Gratitude Ventures 的投资管理业务——两者有很多相似之处。我们有母基金（fund of funds）业务，做直接投资，也在二级市场（secondaries）上很活跃。

turns.en: And a lot of those tools were ones that we used at SUV capital as well. And so I think there's a lot of merit in having an investment platform that is both in LP and a GP and creates relationships along those lines. And then lastly, I think SUVB as a broad organization about Silicon Valley Bank was very community oriented.
turns.zh: 这些工具很多我们在 SVB Capital 时也在用。所以我认为，一个既是 LP 又是 GP 的投资平台是很有价值的，它会顺着这两重身份建立起关系网。最后一点，Silicon Valley Bank 作为一个大机构，是非常有社群导向的。

turns.en: They really thought about how do they show up in the entrepreneurship and technology sector. And so for gradity, we also think about really building an ecosystem in a community within the impact investing mission driven space. So yeah, lots of similarities. And I think culturally it was a great organization.
turns.zh: 他们真的会去思考：在创业和科技这个圈子里，我们该以什么姿态出现。所以在 Gratitude，我们同样在想怎么在影响力投资（impact investing）、使命驱动这个领域里搭建一个生态和社群。是的，相似之处很多。而且从文化上讲，那是一家很棒的机构。

turns.en: People were very mission driven at that time. And so yeah, lots of learnings. A lot of people talk about ecosystem building in our industry. But it's something that's extremely tough to do. And then when you think about family offices, what's the saying? When you meet one family office, you just meet one family office.
turns.zh: 那时候大家都很有使命感，所以我从中学到了很多。我们这个行业里很多人都在谈生态建设（ecosystem building），但这事做起来极难。再说到家族办公室，那句话怎么说来着？你认识了一家家族办公室，你就只认识了这一家。

turns.en: Could you talk to us about kind of the history and the inspiration for a gratitude ventures and kind of started out something more of an investment club and how did it become what it is now? Yeah, absolutely. I mean, we started in 2015. I mean, there was some efforts a little bit earlier than that. But with about a dozen families.
turns.zh: 能不能跟我们讲讲 Gratitude Ventures 的由来和初心？它最早更像是一个投资俱乐部，后来是怎么长成今天这个样子的？当然可以。我们是 2015 年起步的，其实更早之前也有一些尝试，但正式开始时只有十来家家族。

turns.en: So it started very small and we're 10, 15 years later. So it's taken a while to grow the community. And we really wanted to create relatively high bar for folks that were involved that had capacity to invest. That were really committed to this philosophy of investing and wanted to participate and be involved.
turns.zh: 所以起点很小，一晃十年、十五年过去了，把这个社群养大花了不短的时间。我们确实想把门槛定得相对高一些：加入的人要有投资能力，要真正认同这套投资理念，并且愿意参与进来、投入进来。

turns.en: And so all the growth has been very much from referrals and kind of one family at a time. And I think that's built a really great core group. And we're now to point now where there's lots more folks coming our way that it's not as much of a referral one by one. And that's exciting.
turns.zh: 因此所有的增长基本都来自口碑转介，一次一家。我觉得这打造出了一个非常棒的核心群体。而现在我们到了一个节点：主动找上门的人多了很多，不再是一个一个靠转介来。这挺让人兴奋的。

turns.en: And then overall, I think the impacts of sustainability space has gone through an interesting time over the last 10 years where when we started, there was a lack of awareness, right? We were even describing, okay, this is like a different way of investing or operating in business. What do we mean by that?
turns.zh: 整体来看，我认为影响力与可持续这个领域在过去十年经历了一段很有意思的时期。我们刚起步时，市场认知是缺乏的，对吧？我们甚至还得先去解释：好，这是一种不一样的投资方式、不一样的经营企业方式。这到底是什么意思？

turns.en: Is it concessionaries at philanthropy? Or is it for profit investing? And there's a lot of education and skepticism in those early days. And then really there was a massive wave of interest that came kind of coming out of COVID, which was exciting. But I think also has now settled in where we're now 10 years
turns.zh: 它是带有让步性的慈善（concessionary philanthropy）？还是营利性的投资？早年需要做大量科普，也遇到很多质疑。后来疫情之后，真的涌来了一波巨大的关注热潮，很令人振奋。但我觉得现在这股热已经沉淀下来了——我们已经在影响力投资这个周期里走了十年，

turns.en: into I think a cycle within the impact of investing space. And now I think the industry is in a more mature space. But yeah, so there's been a lot of change in the industry and then definitely within our organization. How do you see that change in impact being executed? And something that I'm hearing from some different family offices,
turns.zh: 行业也进入了一个更成熟的阶段。是的，行业里变化很多，我们机构内部的变化更是如此。你怎么看影响力这件事的落地方式？我从一些不同的家族办公室、

turns.en: foundations, and different organizations is that impact now because technology is touching so is ubiquitous with life, essentially. That impact now should be more proactive than reactive. And in some ways when it comes to business angles is like, should these organizations and people have more of a seat
turns.zh: 基金会和各种机构那里听到的一种说法是：既然技术已经渗透到生活的每个角落、几乎无处不在，那么影响力现在就应该是主动的，而不是被动应对的。而从商业角度看，某种程度上问题就变成了：这些机构和人是不是该有更多话语权，

turns.en: at the table on boards or investing? And so I think it's teasing out more than like when I first got introduced to impact investing in kind of 2010 and in other stages. It was more in kind of just the philanthropic side. What have you seen from like your community? Yeah, I mean, we think about it as really being integrated
turns.zh: 在董事会和投资谈判桌上真正占一席之地？所以我觉得这比——我最早接触影响力投资是在 2010 年前后，还有更早的阶段——那时候它更多只在慈善这一侧。你在自己的社群里看到了什么？是这样，我们认为影响力应该是真正贯通的，

turns.en: across all aspects of the capital markets and how you think about running a business. So yeah, there's the idea that impact is the product and service that the business is delivering, that's often how people think about it. Which is important back to what I was saying about the solutions.
turns.zh: 贯穿资本市场的各个环节，也贯穿你经营企业的方式。是的，有一种理解是：影响力就是这家企业交付的产品和服务，大家通常就是这么想的。这一点很重要，也回到我前面说的解决方案（solutions）——

turns.en: Kind of what are we focused on in terms of is it climate or health care, education, financial inclusion? Like those are the products and services and the solutions. And then there's also the how the business operates or how the investor operates and thinking about good governance and the different stakeholders,
turns.zh: 我们聚焦的到底是什么？是气候，还是医疗、教育、普惠金融（financial inclusion）？这些就是产品、服务和解决方案。另一层则是企业怎么运营、投资人怎么运营，要考虑良好的治理，以及各类利益相关方，

turns.en: whether it's your employees, customers, people in the supply chain, to your point, you know, the board representation, is that representative of the end customer that you want to serve. So I think there's more integration that's happening and we really think about it as how do you think about impact
turns.zh: 无论是员工、客户，还是供应链上的人；也如你所说，董事会的构成——它能不能代表你真正想服务的那批终端客户。所以我认为整合正在越来越多地发生，我们真正在思考的是：你该如何看待影响力，

turns.en: throughout the entire ecosystem from the investor to the business to the end customer? I think it was Omidiar basically had two funds, initially like an impact fund with very specific KPIs and then kind of graduated to, we know it when we see it. Yeah. And that from the outside, that sort of makes a lot of sense.
turns.zh: 如何让它贯穿从投资人到企业再到终端客户的整个生态？我记得 Omidyar 一开始基本上有两只基金，一只是 KPI 非常具体的影响力基金，后来慢慢演进成“我们看到了自然认得出来”。是的。而且站在外面看，这个逻辑其实很有道理。

turns.en: That, you know, a family office, you're looking to put your money to work for good. And it's a little too cumbersome and narrow to force everything into measurable KPIs when like you meet a founder and they're doing something you really believe in and can see that it's going to do good for the world. Absolutely.
turns.zh: 作为一个家族办公室，你想让自己的钱去做好事。可当你遇到一位创始人，他做的事你真心认同，你也看得出它会对世界有益，这时候非要把一切塞进可量化的 KPI 里，就显得太笨重、太狭窄了。完全同意。

turns.en: How does that jive with this sort of very formal ESG universe? Like how do the gratitude families approach things versus, you know, when I think about like a Denmark, like foreign investment strategy, right? Like are we putting too many limitations on getting good done?
turns.zh: 那这和整套非常正式的 ESG 体系怎么对得上？Gratitude 的这些家族处理问题的方式，跟我想到某种 Denmark 式的外资投资策略时相比，差别在哪？我们是不是给“把好事做成”加了太多限制？

turns.en: Yeah, and obviously not sticking for the overall industry in terms of how it should be done. Because I do think there is merit in the measurement and the KPIs and we definitely live through a period where I think there was some real, you hear about like greenwashing and people, you know,
turns.zh: 是的，当然我不是在替整个行业发言、说这事就该怎么做。因为我确实认为衡量和 KPI 是有价值的，而且我们肯定经历过那么一段时期——你会听到所谓的漂绿（greenwashing），有些人，你知道，

turns.en: more interested in kind of the marketing advantages. And I think there was some merit to that. So I don't want to kind of toss out all the rigor around measurement and metrics. But I do think about it for us when we're underwriting either a manager or a founder. It's much more about aligning on the philosophical approach,
turns.zh: 更在意的是营销上的好处。我觉得那种说法是有道理的。所以我不想把围绕衡量和指标的所有严谨性都一并丢掉。但对我们来说，在尽调（underwrite）一位基金管理人或一位创始人时，我更看重的是在理念层面能不能对齐，

turns.en: the ethos of the business, what they're why, right? Like what's driving them? Because to me, they're going to go off and run their business. They're going to decide who to invest in and how to operate on a day to day. And the metrics are going to be in the rear view, right?
turns.zh: 这家企业的气质，他们的“为什么”，对吧？到底是什么在驱动他们？因为在我看来，他们转身就会去经营自己的公司，他们要决定投谁、每天怎么运营，而那些指标只会留在后视镜里，对吧？

turns.en: But we want to be aligning with people that I believe are really using the tools that they're disposal to, you know, again, align with the ways that we want to invest in our capital to ultimately move in the world. And I think, you know, for some of our families that sometimes come to this space
turns.zh: 但我们希望与这样的人结盟：我确信他们真的在用手上的一切工具，去契合我们希望资金被投放的方式，最终在这个世界上推动改变。而且我认为，对我们的一些家族来说——他们有时进入这个领域，

turns.en: maybe more from a philanthropic background where they're used to saying, I want to use my philanthropy to solve, you know, an education gap or something in health care and so they want to do their impact investing very narrowly focused on solving that issue. And we don't invest that way, right?
turns.zh: 可能更多是慈善背景出身，他们习惯说：我要用我的慈善资金去解决教育鸿沟，或者医疗领域的某个问题——于是他们希望自己的影响力投资非常窄地聚焦在解决那一个议题上。但我们不是这么投的，对吧？

turns.en: We're investing across different thematic areas. What we're really trying to say is we want to identify those best GPs and founders that are building profitable, economically viable and impactful solutions across different issue areas and really demonstrate that that's possible.
turns.zh: 我们是跨多个主题领域投资的。我们真正想表达的是：我们要找出那些最优秀的 GP 和创始人，他们在不同议题领域里打造既盈利、又在经济上站得住脚、同时有影响力的解决方案，并且真真切切地证明这是可行的。

turns.en: And so it is a shift sometimes for our investors to get comfortable with that approach when they might be really focused on one narrow impact area. But that's been our approach. What tactics have you employed to be able to stay, provide rich, whether it's content, services, insights to your community?
turns.zh: 所以对我们的投资人来说，当他们原本可能非常专注于某一个狭窄的影响力领域时，要适应这套打法有时是一种转变。但这一直是我们的做法。你们用了哪些办法，才能持续为社群提供丰富的内容、服务和洞察？

turns.en: And what have you learned, like, yeah, what have you used and what have you learned over this time? Yeah, I mean, I think in the early days what was really important is, so we have other co-founders to the organization that were further on in their career. They had already found success as entrepreneurs and investment managers
turns.zh: 这段时间里你们又学到了什么？嗯，我觉得早期最关键的一点是——我们机构的其他几位联合创始人职业生涯走得更靠前，他们作为创业者和投资管理人都已经取得了成功，

turns.en: and really decided to lead with their own capital and time and credibility. I think that was really important in the early days for other families and high-knit worth investors to see similar people making this shift, again, putting their capital, their social capital in this direction.
turns.zh: 并且真的决定率先投入自己的资金、时间和信誉。我认为这在早期非常重要：让其他家族和高净值（high-net-worth）投资人看到和自己相似的人正在做这个转向，把自己的资金、自己的社会资本投向这个方向。

turns.en: And so that, I think, built a really strong foundation of a community that was peers, right? That there was a shared trust, credibility that they felt like they were doing it together and that it wasn't me telling them this is the way to do it or pitching some ideas really much more of us in this together and learning by doing.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得这就打下了一个非常坚实的基础：一个由同辈组成的社群，彼此之间有共同的信任和信誉，大家觉得是在一起做这件事，而不是我在告诉他们“就该这么干”，或者在推销什么点子——更多是我们同舟共济、边做边学。

turns.en: And I think that continues to be a really important ethos of our community. And I think along the way also showing up with an idea of how do we make sure we're being helpful to people in the community, right? And that's always been an important cultural item is how can we be helpful?
turns.zh: 我认为这一点至今仍是我们社群非常重要的精神内核。而且一路走来，我们始终带着一个问题出现：怎么才能真正帮到社群里的人？这一直是一条重要的文化准则——我们能帮上什么忙？

turns.en: What are you interested in? What are you trying to solve? What are you grappling with? How do we make important, helpful connections right out of the gate? And we still today, our investors, our community members, the value is the community. They connect with each other outside of the things we put together and that's really helpful.
turns.zh: 你对什么感兴趣？你想解决什么问题？你正在跟什么难题较劲？我们怎么从一开始就牵上真正重要、真正有用的线？直到今天，我们的投资人、我们的社群成员都说：价值就在社群本身。他们会在我们组织的活动之外彼此连接，这真的非常有帮助。

turns.en: And I think you just have to create a high bar where you're creating a community of people that show up, that want to connect with each other. So we've never had a KPI on like number growth, right? It's always been, you know, who's the right people we want in the community?
turns.zh: 我觉得你就是得设一个高门槛，打造一个人人愿意到场、愿意彼此连接的社群。所以我们从来没有把“人数增长”当成 KPI，对吧？一直都是：我们希望进社群的，是对的人。

turns.en: How do we make sure we're getting exposure to them and how do we make sure that it's valuable to answer and involve in the community? Is there a commonality or common thread between every family or high net worth individual who joins? Yeah, similar. There was much more of a focus on people who came from a business and finance background.
turns.zh: 我们怎么确保能接触到这些人，又怎么确保他们参与社群、投入社群是有价值的？加入的每一个家族或高净值个人之间，有没有什么共性或共同的主线？有，比较相似。早期我们更侧重来自商业和金融背景的人。

turns.en: So we would say early on, hey, we don't necessarily want to teach people how to think about investing or operate a business. We're going to get them to ship their mindset around what does it mean to invest in operator business if you're solving for yes, profit and return and solving for important social and environmental solutions.
turns.zh: 所以我们早期会说：嘿，我们并不一定要教人怎么思考投资、怎么经营企业。我们要做的是调整他们的心态——如果你在同时求解“利润和回报”以及“重要的社会与环境解决方案”，那么投资一家企业、经营一家企业到底意味着什么。

turns.en: So the core of the community definitely comes from that business and finance background. But that's expanded beyond that now. I think that foundation was set and now we're much more interested on how do we bring the right people and that are motivated to move capital that also have different perspectives too.
turns.zh: 所以社群的核心确实来自商业和金融背景。但现在这已经扩展到那个范围之外了。我认为那个基础已经打好，如今我们更关心的是：怎么把对的人带进来——既有推动资金流动的意愿，又能带来不同的视角。

turns.en: I mean, there's extreme value in people that are coming from different backgrounds and industries and outside of the business and finance world. So yeah, that through line is still there, but not as critical today. The one that's critical today is the action orientation.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，来自不同背景、不同行业、商业和金融圈之外的人，价值是极大的。所以是的，那条主线还在，但今天已经没那么关键了。今天真正关键的是行动导向。

turns.en: We do not want to be a community of people that just sit around and talk about these ideas. We always had a view of we need to put capital to work, we need to learn by doing and so that continues to be an important through line that ultimately we're about moving capital.
turns.zh: 我们不希望成为一个大家只是坐在那里空谈理念的社群。我们一直认为：得让资金真正投出去，得边做边学。所以这始终是另一条重要的主线——归根结底，我们做的是让资本流动起来。

turns.en: You're in a very unique situation where you're hearing constantly about what these families actually are interested in. And I see that in the different products that you now offer. So maybe you could give an example of sort of like a new product that is available to the group
turns.zh: 你所处的位置非常独特：你随时都能听到这些家族真正感兴趣的是什么，我也能从你们现在提供的不同产品里看出来。那能不能举个例子，说说面向这个群体推出的某个新产品，

turns.en: and where that came from or why you decided to add it to what you provide. Yeah, I mean, that's definitely an important part of how we think about the synergy of the community and the investment business. I mean, I'll use the word tension, but I mean, there is this tension of interest from the investors and the community
turns.zh: 它是怎么来的，或者说你们为什么决定把它加进产品线的？嗯，这确实是我们思考“社群与投资业务如何协同”时很重要的一部分。我可能会用“张力”这个词——投资人和社群的兴趣诉求，和我们认为真正该做、该往哪儿投资金之间，

turns.en: and what we think makes sense to actually do and how, okay, capital towards it. And we want to bring that input in because it's really valuable, but it shouldn't be the driver of every decision we make. Oh, I would love to hear when you recommend they not invest in as well.
turns.zh: 确实存在这种张力。我们想把这种输入纳进来，因为它真的很有价值，但它不应该成为我们每一个决策的驱动力。哦，那我也很想听听你们建议他们“不要投”的时候。

turns.en: Yes, yes. And there's just the general idea of behavioral finance and where trends go and what people are interested in. So yeah, I mean, we see that in our little community as a sample size of what's going on broadly in the investor ecosystem.
turns.zh: 对，对。这里面还有一层，就是行为金融（behavioral finance）的一般规律——趋势往哪儿走、大家在关注什么。所以我们把这个小小的社群当作一个样本，来看整个投资人生态里正在发生什么。

turns.en: But yeah, I mean, an example of a product that came together actually last year, which was a really challenging time for the solar industry, as we ended up putting together a yield co focused on investing in small commercial solar and storage products projects in primarily low income and energy communities in the US.
turns.zh: 不过，举个产品真正成型的例子——就在去年，那是光伏行业非常艰难的一段时间，我们最终组建了一只 YieldCo，专注于投资美国小型工商业光伏加储能项目，主要落在低收入社区和能源社区。

turns.en: And it was a match of an area that our investors were interested in, which was kind of a yield generating lower risk product relative to our more traditional venture and private equity products.
turns.zh: 这正好对上我们投资人感兴趣的方向：相比我们更传统的风投和私募股权产品，这是一类能产生收益、风险更低的产品。

turns.en: And then us seeing a gap in the marketplace where, you know, smaller commercial solar and storage projects weren't getting financed by the larger investment thumbs and where we could bring kind of worth individuals and family offices into that ecosystem where they were kind of right size from a check size perspective.
turns.zh: 同时我们也看到了市场上的一个空白：规模较小的工商业光伏和储能项目拿不到大型投资机构的钱；而我们可以把高净值个人和家族办公室带进这个生态——从出资体量上看，他们的大小刚刚好。

turns.en: So I think that was a great example where we were able to educate our community on the opportunities that even amidst all the changes happening in the renewable energy space and bring a pool of capital that was really helpful to a part of the market that was under served.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得这是一个很好的例子：即便在可再生能源领域发生那么多变化的当口，我们依然能给社群讲清楚机会在哪儿，并且汇集起一笔资本，去真正帮到市场上服务不足的那一块。

turns.en: Is there anything that you are hearing a lot of people are interested in that you are advising against? I mean, one of the topics that it's changed names, but kind of nature-based solutions, natural capital, investing in biodiversity. I mean, incredibly important. And there's elements of what we do that touch that theme.
turns.zh: 有没有什么是你听到很多人很感兴趣、但你却在劝他们别碰的？有一个话题，名字换过好几次，大致就是基于自然的解决方案（nature-based solutions）、自然资本（natural capital）、生物多样性投资。这东西极其重要，我们做的事情里也有一部分会碰到这个主题。

turns.en: I think that there's a lot of interest from families of figuring out how to allocate capital there.
turns.zh: 我确实感觉到，很多家族都很有兴趣去弄清楚：该怎么把资金配置到那里。

turns.en: And our view today is that the ecosystem around the investment opportunities is still emerging and pretty nascent. And so there needs to be some more work on developing what are the investment products, what is kind of the risk return profile of those investment products.
turns.zh: 但我们今天的看法是，围绕这些投资机会的生态仍在形成中，还相当早期。所以还需要下更多功夫去打磨：投资产品到底长什么样，这些产品的风险收益特征（risk-return profile）又是什么。

turns.en: So that's one where we're kind of taking that interest in and saying, here's some maybe some other ways to express that interest in some existing investment opportunities that have a more clear kind of risk return profile. But yeah, that would be one that comes to mind.
turns.zh: 所以这一块我们的做法是：先接住这份兴趣，然后告诉他们，也许可以用另外一些方式来安放这份兴趣——去投那些风险收益特征更清晰的现有机会。是的，这是我马上能想到的一个。

turns.en: Is there any kind of growing impact thesis amongst your team and the community on how to approach data center investments and also data centers overall, right, what could be the indirect results of more of them popping up?
turns.zh: 在你们团队和社群里，关于如何看待数据中心投资、乃至数据中心整体——也就是数据中心越建越多可能带来哪些间接后果——有没有正在成形的影响力投资论点？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, it made it broad, not the question a little bit. There's what's happening right because of AI is this growth in energy demand, right, which has its drawbacks or its concerns or its questions.
turns.zh: 嗯，这是个大问题，让我把它收窄一点。当下因为 AI 而发生的事，是能源需求的增长，对吧？这背后有它的弊端、有它的隐忧，也有它的疑问。

turns.en: But in some ways, it's continuing to put wind in the sales around the renewable energy space, which was having more headwinds given the administration view on some of the areas around wind and solar, for example.
turns.zh: 但从某些方面看，它在持续给可再生能源这个领域鼓风加帆——而这个领域本来正遭遇更多逆风，比如现任政府在风电、光伏等议题上的态度。

turns.en: So that's been really interesting where, you know, because of the data center boom and AI demand, you know, renewable energies kind of getting pulled through and that's a good thing, right, that's a positive continue to have that industry and those technologies mature and scale.
turns.zh: 所以这一点非常有意思：因为数据中心的热潮和 AI 的需求，可再生能源算是被硬生生拉了一把。这是好事，对吧？这是一股正向力量，能让这个行业和这些技术继续成熟、继续上规模。

turns.en: But there is some questions on, you know, how do we as a society deal with just this massive growth in energy demand. And do we have the technologies to really scale up in a responsible way? And our view would be, you know, hopefully more renewable sources versus our current non-renewable sources.
turns.zh: 但也确实有问题：作为一个社会，我们该怎么应对能源需求如此巨大的增长？我们手上有没有那种能以负责任的方式真正扩张的技术？我们的看法是，希望更多来自可再生能源，而不是我们现在依赖的不可再生能源。

turns.en: And what's the timeline of, for example, getting nuclear to a place where it's commercially viable when the energy demand is happening yesterday. And so those disconnects, I think, are things that we grapple with. Yeah, it's like throw them in space then or throw them underwater. That won't have impact on things. And switching gears.
turns.zh: 再比如，把核能推到商业可行的那一天，时间表会是什么样？可变故是能源需求“昨天”就已经来了。所以这些错配，我认为正是我们要反复琢磨的难题。是啊，那不如干脆把它们扔到太空里去，或者沉到水底，这样就不会有影响了。我们换个话题。

turns.en: Prep conversation, we also spoke about your presence of investing in emerging managers. I believe it's around 30 plus managers with a dedicated pool of funding. Could you just walk us through that program and the process, what it looks like?
turns.zh: 在录前的沟通里，我们也聊到你们在新锐管理人（emerging managers）上的投入。我记得是有 30 多位管理人，配了一笔专项资金池。能不能带我们走一遍这个计划和它的流程，具体是什么样子？

turns.en: Absolutely. Yeah, it's always been and we'll continue to be an important part of how we think about allocating to managers. We do believe that there's real value in emerging managers from an alpha perspective, from building the ecosystem, from cultivating new talent into asset management.
turns.zh: 当然。是的，这一直是我们思考如何配置基金管理人时的重要组成部分，未来也会继续是。我们确实相信新锐管理人有实实在在的价值：从超额收益（alpha）的角度，从建设生态的角度，从为资产管理行业培育新人才的角度。

turns.en: And so it will always be an important part of our investing for those reasons. And then there's also some real benefits to us in terms of the relationships that we develop with those emerging managers. It is different when you are a first check into a fun one of an emerging manager, that relationship doesn't fade very easily.
turns.zh: 正因如此，它永远会是我们投资中的关键一环。此外，我们与这些新锐管理人建立的关系，对我们自己也有实实在在的好处。当你是一位新锐管理人一期基金的第一张支票时，感觉是不一样的，那种关系不会轻易变淡。

turns.en: It's a really important one. And so that is real benefits where we're able to bring those managers into our community and our community benefits from learning from those managers. They show up. They're super engaged and that's really valuable.
turns.zh: 那是一段非常重要的关系。所以好处很实在：我们能把这些管理人带进社群，而社群也能从他们身上学到东西。他们会到场，参与度极高，这非常有价值。

turns.en: And then for us on the investing side, we do a lot of co-investing with those managers and learn from their sector expertise or maybe they invest at different stages than we do. So there's ancillary benefits to not only kind of the core value proposition of investing in emerging managers. And it's evolved over time.
turns.zh: 而在投资这一侧，我们和这些管理人做了很多联合投资（co-invest），从他们的行业专长里学习，也可能他们投的阶段和我们不同。所以除了投资新锐管理人这个核心价值主张之外，还有不少附加收益。这块也在随时间演进。

turns.en: I think it is part of the market that ebbs and flows as there's more bearishness or bolusness around asset management. And so we're kind of coming out of a period where I think it was really difficult for emerging managers.
turns.zh: 我认为这是市场中会潮起潮落的一部分，取决于大家对资产管理是更悲观还是更乐观。所以我们刚刚走出的那一段，对新锐管理人来说确实非常艰难。

turns.en: I'm optimistic that that's going to shift over the next couple of years just as people are seeing the value of being invested in venture consistently through a long period of time. And if you weren't invested in venture in the early 2000s, mid 2000s, you missed what's happening today.
turns.zh: 我很乐观，未来几年这种情况会转变，因为大家正在看到长期、持续地投在风投里的价值。如果你在 2000 年代初、2000 年代中期没有投风投，你就错过了今天正在发生的一切。

turns.en: And so I think people are saying, OK, I want to make sure I'm invested in venture consistently. And a lot of the larger mainstream funds are capacity constraint. It's a different relationship, obviously.
turns.zh: 所以我认为大家在说：好，我得确保自己持续投在风投里。而很多更大的主流基金是有容量上限的，那显然也是一种不一样的关系。

turns.en: And so if you're going to build a venture program having some exploded emerging managers, I think people will continue to see that as valuable. I think that will be an easier environment for emerging managers coming over the next couple of years and it's been over the past two.
turns.zh: 所以如果你要搭建一个风投组合，配一部分新锐管理人，我认为大家会继续觉得这有价值。我认为未来几年对新锐管理人来说，环境会比过去两年更容易一些。

turns.en: Now we're going to take a quick break to speak with our sponsor. On the show today, we have our stellar partner and industry expert Shane Gowdy, leader of Sidley's venture funds practice. And now host of the podcast talk, VC, we highly recommend you listen.
turns.zh: 现在我们稍作休息，去和我们的赞助商聊几句。今天来到节目的是我们出色的合作伙伴、行业专家 Shane Goudey，他负责 Sidley 的风险基金（venture funds）业务，同时也主持播客 Talk VC，我们非常推荐你去听。

turns.en: The other one I wanted to ask you about is the one big beautiful bill act rewriting everything around qualified QSPS. Yeah. And what we should keep in mind as a sort of VC LP audience. Yeah, I think that we're in a world of secondaries now.
turns.zh: 另一个我想问你的，是 One Big Beautiful Bill Act 把围绕合格小企业股票（QSBS）的规则全都重写了一遍。是啊，那作为一档面向 VC LP 的节目，我们的听众该记住什么？嗯，我认为我们现在身处一个二级市场（secondaries）的世界。

turns.en: And so I think the thing that people lose sight of is that those are just dangerous to QSPS treatment. And so the minute that a security becomes a secondary security, any ability to claim it from a QSPS standpoint goes away. So while there is tremendous attractiveness and a lot of the secondary opportunities out there, I think that too.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得大家容易忽略的是：这些交易对 QSBS 的税务待遇是有杀伤力的。一旦某只证券变成了二级市场证券，任何从 QSBS 角度去主张优惠的可能性就消失了。所以尽管市面上很多二级市场机会有着巨大的吸引力，我也认为——

turns.en: And a lot of it is these businesses are just so big QSPS isn't even a thing, right? So some of that activity just doesn't, QSPS doesn't even enter the radar screen that's not even a bullet. Did they ever have a 50 million under it? Yeah, exactly. So it's just not even something we think about. Yeah.
turns.zh: 而且很多情况下，这些公司体量已经大到 QSBS 根本不成其为议题了，对吧？所以有些交易里，QSBS 连雷达都上不了，它甚至都不算清单上的一条。这些公司是不是从来就没有低于过 5000 万美元那条线？对，正是如此。所以这压根就不是我们会去想的事。嗯。

turns.en: But as you start to plan for even things like warehousing, this is a lot of what's going on in the fund raises these days. It's just because of the rapidity of the deal opportunities is happening in advance of a fundraising closing.
turns.zh: 但一旦你开始为像“先行囤积”（warehousing）这类事情做筹划——这正是当下募资中大量发生的情况——原因就在于交易机会来得太快，往往在一轮融资正式关账之前就已经出现了。

turns.en: You know, a lot of times the management company or management company or one of the managing directors or some affiliated entity, you may warehouse the investments and that's as soon as that thing gets transferred into the fund, there goes the QSPS on it.
turns.zh: 很多时候是由管理公司，或者某位董事总经理，或者某个关联实体先把这些投资囤起来；而一旦这些资产被转入基金，它身上的 QSBS 资格也就跟着没了。

turns.en: So I think it's just being mindful and God forbid we go down the rabbit hole of it, is carry QSPS eligible? I only bring it up just to be really funny. But those are the kinds of things that, and it's not a nothing issue from a tax perspective.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得关键是要留心——千万别让我们钻进那个兔子洞：业绩分成（carry）到底能不能享受 QSBS？我提这个纯粹是为了搞笑。但这一类问题，从税务角度看绝不是无关痛痒的小事。

turns.en: So, you know, a little bit of his same as it ever was just in terms of like true emerging early stage kind of companies and how to manage your ability to continue to have QSPS status. But again, in a world where some of this access is just happening through secondary and other different channels, it's just being aware of the playbook.
turns.zh: 所以说，有点“一切照旧”的味道——对那些真正早期的新兴公司而言，问题依然是怎么保住你持续享有 QSBS 资格的能力。但同样，在一个部分投资准入是通过二级市场和其他不同渠道实现的世界里，你要做的就是熟悉这套打法。

turns.en: And you know, how to, you know, whether the one big beautiful bill will solve much or any of that is still up for debate. But I think it is just mindful about, you know, just the tax advantageousness of how you move through the world and doing these investments.
turns.zh: 至于 One Big Beautiful Bill 能不能解决其中大部分甚至任何一部分，目前仍有争议。但我认为，重要的是时刻留意：你在市场中怎么行动、怎么做这些投资，才能在税务上更有优势。

turns.en: QSPS is an element of it, but we've seen just from a planning perspective, things like management of the three year long term capital gains period for the holding of stock.
turns.zh: QSBS 只是其中一个要素。但从规划的角度，我们还看到过诸如如何管理持股的三年长期资本利得（long-term capital gains）期限这类事情。

turns.en: And how does a GP manage, you know, that kind of opportunity for themselves in that, you know, the kinds of things that we're seeing GPs do with being able to take in kind distributions with everybody else is getting cash so that if it's an under two year or an under three year stock they can hold on to it, tack that holding period.
turns.zh: GP 该怎么为自己管理这样的机会？我们看到 GP 在做的一类操作是：在别人都拿现金的时候，他选择接受实物分配（in-kind distribution）。这样一来，如果是持有不满两年或不满三年的股票，他就可以继续拿着，把持有期接续计算下去。

turns.en: And then when they decide to sell it, you know, have long term capital gains or doing things on the allocations, it's not even just QSPS.
turns.zh: 等到他们决定卖出的时候，就能享受长期资本利得税率；或者在分配比例上做文章——这些已经不单单是 QSBS 的问题了。

turns.en: It's really a lot of these things that, you know, regenerate out of the tax piece that, you know, the savvy really good fund managers are keeping track of and their their counsel is right behind them or frankly more often way ahead of them.
turns.zh: 真的有很多这类从税务环节衍生出来的问题，那些精明、真正优秀的基金管理人在盯着；而他们的法律顾问要么紧随其后，坦白说，更多时候是远远走在他们前面。

turns.en: So, you know, but, but as we counsel, you know, the funds that we, you know, bring online, like when we talk about warehousing, like this is, this is the kind of topics we talk about.
turns.zh: 所以，当我们在为那些新接手的基金提供顾问服务时，比如聊到先行囤积，这就是我们会讨论的那类话题。

turns.en: It's not just, you know, it can be regulatory issues because, you know, secondary securities and a venture fund is a bad thing, this is not necessarily, but if you get basket like warehousing could be that, but there's an exception for it.
turns.zh: 这不只是税务问题，也可能是监管问题——因为二级市场证券出现在一只风投基金里通常是件坏事。这不必然，但如果搞过了头，先行囤积就可能变成那种情况，好在它有一项例外规定。

turns.en: So, it's, it's just a lot of counseling on some of this stuff. So, I'm hopeful that some of the elements of the big beautiful bill, you know, maybe loosen some of the grip on some of the restrictions for QSPS.
turns.zh: 所以这些事情里有大量是需要提供咨询和辅导的。我倒是希望 big beautiful bill 里的某些条款，也许能松动一下对 QSBS 那些限制的紧箍。

turns.en: I think that's possible, but we'll see. It's still all up in the air at this moment and I think people are still, you know, trying to get the car before the horse on some of this activity. And frankly, QSPS just becomes the fifth consideration in a list that's very, very long.
turns.zh: 我觉得这是有可能的，但还得看。眼下一切都还悬着，而且我认为在一些操作上，大家还是在把车套在马前面，本末倒置。坦白讲，QSBS 最终只是那张非常非常长的清单上排在第五位的考量。

turns.en: Well, I can see how Council ends up easily helping you avoid some of these giant potholes and, you know, it really matters who you're working with. Yeah. You lead this practice. Why would you recommend that GPs choose to do their fund formation work with you?
turns.zh: 我完全能理解，法律顾问是怎么轻轻松松帮你绕开这些大坑的，而且和你合作的人是谁真的很重要。是啊。你负责这块业务，那你会推荐 GP 把基金设立（fund formation）的活儿交给你们做的理由是什么？

turns.en: Yeah. How long we have? No, no. So, I think we keep it simple, right? I came here over two years ago because, you know, a lot of the, a lot of the venture landscape from a legal representation standpoint just became about kind of vacuum sucking in a lot of different relationships and not really about the service element of it all.
turns.zh: 我们还有多长时间？不不。我觉得我们把事情做得很简单，对吧？我两年多前来到这里，是因为从法律代理的角度看，风投这个圈子里很多东西变成了拼命把各种关系一股脑吸进来，而不再真正关乎服务本身。

turns.en: So, I think that we, it's idly, have crafted the venture funds practice to be client serving for one. And I don't think enough, enough law firms do that. I think it's about pelt on the wall. I don't think it's about the relationships with the LPs. I don't think it's, or with the GPs and the LPs.
turns.zh: 所以我认为，我们 Sidley 把风险基金业务打造成第一要务就是服务客户。我不觉得有足够多的律所在这么做。我觉得他们干的是往墙上乱甩、看什么能粘住，我不认为他们真正在乎和 LP 的关系，也不认为在乎和 GP、LP 的关系。

turns.en: So, it's purpose-built by design. It's really concierge service for a venture fund. And just the ability of a firm like Sidley to have not only just the fund formation because our, our slice of our funds practice is 150 plus lawyers and the Sidley funds practices doing hedge and private equity and real estate and credit and, you know, all sorts of really, really interesting things under the asset management.
turns.zh: 所以它是从设计之初就为特定目的打造的，本质上是为一只风投基金提供管家式（concierge）服务。而像 Sidley 这样一家律所的能力，不止于基金设立——我们这一块基金业务就有 150 多位律师，Sidley 的基金业务整体还覆盖对冲基金、私募股权、房地产、信贷，以及资产管理之下各种非常有意思的领域。

turns.en: And this venture funds practice is sort of the newest kid on the block, but it is very fundamental for what the firm is doing from a venture ecosystem representation standpoint.
turns.zh: 而风险基金这块业务算是街区里最新来的那个孩子。但从代表整个风投生态的角度看，它对这家律所正在做的事情又是非常根本性的。

turns.en: And, you know, we have an incredible emerging companies practice. I'm led by, you know, some of the most amazing Titans in the industry, but you really need to compliment that company side representation with the fund side.
turns.zh: 我们有一支极强的新兴公司（emerging companies）业务团队，由行业里一些最了不起的大咖带领。但你确实需要用基金这一侧的能力，去补足公司这一侧的代理。

turns.en: And so, we here have been able to marry that. Now, that's a, that's a DNA that exists in other firms, but if you don't compliment that with world class regulatory and tax and credit and, you know, VC financing and all this other expertise and not just having one person that does it, but having a complete complimentary team that really can be again from that client service standpoint, you're not waiting in line for 300 other funds to get an answer on this.
turns.zh: 所以我们在这一点上做到了两者的结合。当然，这种基因别的律所也有，但如果你不用世界级的监管、税务、信贷、VC 融资以及其他各种专业能力去补足它，如果你不是只有一个人干这活，而是有一整支互补完整的团队——那么从客户服务的角度看，你就真的不用排在另外 300 只基金后面才等到一个答复。

turns.en: You know, we've been very purposeful about the relationships that we've taken on and, you know, we've gotten a lot of really great interest and like, you know, it's fun being the new kid on the block. And, you know, the Sidley name is, you know, one of the Titans of the industry, but not necessarily in the venture space until recently.
turns.zh: 我们在选择接手哪些客户关系上是非常有目的性的，也确实获得了大量很好的关注。当“街区新来的孩子”挺有意思的。Sidley 这个名字是行业里的巨头之一，但直到最近，在风投这个圈子里还不算是。

turns.en: And it's, it's fun for me. This has been the most fun I've ever had in my career to be a business builder and to sit across from VCs every day who that is their job is to build businesses and kind of be able to now find a little kinship with them in doing this.
turns.zh: 对我来说这很有意思。这是我职业生涯里最开心的一段：做一个业务的搭建者，每天坐在 VC 对面——他们的工作就是搭建企业——而如今能在这件事上和他们找到一点同类之感。

turns.en: That personal relationship and that commonality of experience is pretty damn fun. And we just take a practical approach, right?
turns.zh: 那种个人层面的关系和经历上的共通，真的是爽得要命。而我们的做法就是务实，对吧？

turns.en: You know, while Sidley is a massive firm and a lot of people think of massive firms doing things complex and, you know, not being able to meet costs, you know, for us, we're able to keep it simple stupid, you know, be very targeted about with our advice and our approach.
turns.zh: 虽然 Sidley 是一家巨大的律所，很多人会觉得大所做事复杂、价格上也接不住，但对我们来说，我们能做到“简单点，别搞复杂”（keep it simple, stupid），让建议和打法都非常有的放矢。

turns.en: But then also do it in price that matches really any other firm doing this work, you know, with a sizable practice. So you get really the best of all worlds. And I think that, you know, has been a message that sold really, really well for a lot of people who came with me onto the platform for my prior firm.
turns.zh: 同时价格上又能和任何一家做这类业务、规模可观的律所持平。所以你真的是把各方好处都拿到了。我认为这套说法非常有说服力，很多客户当初就是随着我从上一家律所一起转到这个平台上的。

turns.en: But, you know, now our brand new clients to Sidley and whether that's through brand new introduction or maybe through another partner here at Sidley. It's just, you know, when you have a fire on a mountaintop, people tend to look and that, and that for me has been just tremendous opportunity for us to succeed.
turns.zh: 但现在他们成了 Sidley 全新的客户，无论是通过全新的引荐，还是通过 Sidley 这里的另一位合伙人。就像山顶上点起一堆火，人们总会望过来——对我来说，这就是我们得以成功的巨大机会。

turns.en: And, you know, where we would be delighted to work with any venture fund manager of any size, because we really do. We represent funds that are $10 million, first time funds to ones with, you know, $5 billion plus.
turns.zh: 而且我们非常乐意与任何规模的风投基金管理人合作，我们是认真的。我们代理的基金，小到 1000 万美元的首期基金，大到 50 亿美元以上。

turns.en: So it runs the full gamut, and because of all this other expertise that we have, we're able to meet kind of the meter of what RBCs expect of us.
turns.zh: 所以整个光谱我们都覆盖了。而正因为我们还有那么多其他专业能力，我们才能达到 VC 对我们期待的那个标准。

turns.en: Thank you for joining us on the show, Shane. If you're a GP or LP looking for expert guidance on fund formation and venture capital legal matters, you can visit Sidley's website, sidel.com, and now back to our LP interview. Given the mix of fund level investments, direct investments, what kind of check sizes are we talking about?
turns.zh: Shane，感谢你来到我们的节目。如果你是正在寻找基金设立和风险投资法律事务专业指导的 GP 或 LP，可以访问 Sidley 的网站 sidley.com。现在我们回到 LP 访谈。考虑到你们是基金层面投资和直接投资混合的模式，我们说的出资体量大概是什么量级？

turns.en: Like, I think a lot of folks will say this is like fees on fees, and they don't really respect the work that these managers are providing. But I think when you put numbers to it, it sort of starts to make a little more sense where you realize this is actually cheap labor. Yeah.
turns.zh: 我觉得很多人会说这就是“费用之上再收费用”（fees on fees），他们并不真正尊重这些管理人提供的工作。但我认为，一旦你把数字摆出来，事情就开始更有道理了——你会意识到这其实是廉价的人力。嗯。

turns.en: Can you give us a little sense of what your LP commits are like, what you're looking to deploy in the individual co investments or follow on? Yeah, I mean, we, so we do have a view of trying to be accessible. That's always been important.
turns.zh: 能不能让我们大致了解一下你们的 LP 承诺出资是什么水平，以及在单笔联合投资或后续跟投上打算投多少？嗯，我们的想法是要让人容易参与进来，这一点一直很重要。

turns.en: We recognize that the type of investing we do, both from our philosophy as well as investing in private markets and primarily in venture. That's a small part of any allocator's allocation, right? It's kind of a percent on a percent.
turns.zh: 我们清楚，我们所做的这类投资——无论从我们的理念来看，还是从投私募市场、且主要投风投来看——在任何配置者的组合里都只占很小一块，对吧？基本上是“百分比里再抠出一个百分比”。

turns.en: And so our view has been we want to get people involved, build trust, and take a long view on those relationships. So, well, our investors investing, we're from 250,000 on the low end up to a few million in our strategies. We have a multiple product approach to our platform.
turns.zh: 所以我们的想法是：先把人带进来，建立信任，用长期的眼光经营这些关系。我们投资人的出资额，低的一端是 25 万美元，高的一端在我们的各类策略里能到几百万美元。

turns.en: So the idea is that families can invest in multiple products that are complimentary versus having kind of one dedicated venture fund, for example. So that's kind of how we think about bringing our investors in ultimately how that shows up to our investments is on our early stage really seed series A.
turns.zh: 我们的平台采取多产品路线。思路是：家族可以投资多个互补的产品，而不是只押一只专门的风投基金。这就是我们把投资人带进来的方式。而这一点最终体现在我们的投资上，就是在早期——基本上是种子轮和 A 轮——

turns.en: We're typically investing about half a million to a million in rounds of three to 10 million. So we're not typically leading or one of the largest investors, but want to be meaningful to the cap table.
turns.zh: 我们通常在 300 万到 1000 万美元规模的轮次里投 50 万到 100 万美元。所以我们一般不领投，也不是最大的投资人之一，但希望在股权结构表（cap table）上有分量。

turns.en: And then on the fund manager side really can range from half a million to a million, which can be meaningful for a early stage fund one venture fund manager up to a few million for more steps. Maybe non venture private market manager.
turns.zh: 而在基金管理人这一侧，出资可以从 50 万到 100 万美元——对一位早期阶段、一期基金的风投管理人来说，这已经很有分量——上到几百万美元，对应更成熟、也许是非风投的私募市场管理人。

turns.en: And I think that is a place where we feel like we have a strategy that makes sense where we can be collaborative in the ways that we invest and meaningful to either the cap table or the LP base for the fund manager. So I don't imagine that shifting dramatically over the next few years.
turns.zh: 我觉得在这个位置上，我们的策略是说得通的：我们的投资方式可以是协作型的，同时对基金管理人来说，无论是在股权结构表上还是在其 LP 群体里，都足够有分量。所以我不认为未来几年这会发生剧烈变化。

turns.en: I think we feel like we're kind of in the right place in terms of where we play. Do you have any examples of how, whether it's from the community or outside voices that it's led you to an opportunity that you all learn aware of?
turns.zh: 我们认为自己所处的这个位置是对的。有没有什么例子——不管来自社群内部还是外部的声音——把你们引向了一个原本你们并不知晓的机会？

turns.en: For sure. We, one that we've been highlighting recently is we had been interested in investing in Fintech and financial inclusion and had struggled to really find kind of the right opportunities in our early stage venture portfolio.
turns.zh: 当然有。最近我们一直在讲的一个例子是：我们一直有兴趣投金融科技（Fintech）和普惠金融，但在早期风投组合里始终很难找到真正合适的机会。

turns.en: And we, a new investor joined the community that was a founder of a Fintech company and got very involved in saying, I'd love to help you guys think through that and help source investments and ultimately source an investment and helped us win that investment.
turns.zh: 后来有一位新投资人加入了社群，他本身是一家金融科技公司的创始人，非常投入地说：我很愿意帮你们把这块想清楚、帮着找项目。最终他真的给我们找来一个项目，还帮我们拿下了这笔投资。

turns.en: And then now as a informal advisor to the company and the companies growing and scaling well, it's a business that helps spring retirement advice to lower middle income Americans.
turns.zh: 现在他还担任这家公司的非正式顾问，而公司发展得很好、扩张得也不错。这是一家为美国中低收入人群送去退休规划建议的公司。

turns.en: And so just a part of the market that hadn't really been addressed and that's one example, but there's many, but when that can happen where someone actually adds value to our process and then more importantly, the entrepreneur, the fund manager that we're investing is like, I really want to continue to work with this person.
turns.zh: 所以这就是市场里一块此前几乎没人认真服务的领域。这只是一个例子，类似的还有很多。而当有人真的能为我们的流程增值，更重要的是，我们投的那位创业者、那位基金管理人也说“我真的很想继续和这个人合作”时——

turns.en: That's a huge differentiation for us in the marketplace. And I think that what I talked about with our portfolio companies often is, there's a lot of the firms that talk about community and having active investors involved and they can add value.
turns.zh: 这对我们在市场上就是巨大的差异化。我经常跟我们的被投企业聊的一点是：市面上有很多机构都在讲社群、讲让投资人积极参与、讲自己能带来价值。

turns.en: And I think what we see is this mission orientation, the alignment around the impact that these companies and fund managers are having, people show up in a different way.
turns.zh: 而我们看到的是这种使命导向——大家围绕这些公司和基金管理人所创造的影响力形成了共识，于是人们以不一样的姿态出现。

turns.en: They show up with, you know, they're more engaged, they're more committed. That mission kind of holds people more accountable to be value added. And so that's been fun to see and I think is an important part of how we operate. Thomas, have you seen an uptick in people investing out of donor advice funds?
turns.zh: 他们参与度更高、投入度更高。那份使命感会让人感到更有责任去真正创造价值。看到这一点很有意思，我认为这也是我们运作方式中很重要的一部分。Thomas，你有没有看到越来越多的人从捐赠人建议基金（donor-advised funds）里出钱做投资？

turns.en: Smiling because yes, the hope of donor advice funds moving into impact investing has been been out there for a long time. I mean, it continues to just grow and grow. Where is the where are people giving you money from?
turns.zh: （笑）是的，“捐赠人建议基金流入影响力投资”这个期待已经存在很久了，而且这个池子还在不断变大。那大家的钱到底是从哪儿给到你的？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, it's, yeah, I know what the latest numbers are in their advice fund. It's definitely over 100 billion. It's probably maybe double that now, but it's a massive amount of capital that, yeah, you would think.
turns.zh: 嗯，我知道捐赠人建议基金最新的数据。它肯定超过 1000 亿美元，现在也许已经是那个数的两倍了。总之是一笔极其庞大的资金，你会觉得——是啊。

turns.en: So this door advice funds are a form of a foundation where people are taking the tax benefit of gifting capital to a donor advice fund. Different from a foundation is they don't have a mandatory distribution. So foundation has a mandatory distribution of 5%.
turns.zh: 捐赠人建议基金其实是基金会的一种形式：人们把资金捐给它，从而获得税收上的好处。它和基金会的区别在于没有强制分配要求，而基金会是必须每年分配 5% 的。

turns.en: They don't really don't advise funds do not have that. So they can continue to grow and grow. You know, these are typically invested in money market funds or passive ETFs. Most of them are managed by fidelity and Vanguard and Charles Schwab. But ultimately, this is philanthropic capital that's supposed to be put to work.
turns.zh: 捐赠人建议基金没有这条规定，所以它可以一直滚、一直涨。这些钱通常投在货币市场基金或者被动型 ETF 里，大部分由 Fidelity、Vanguard 和 Charles Schwab 管理。但归根结底，这是本该被真正用起来的慈善资本。

turns.en: My first hope would be that it actually gets put to work for philanthropic reasons as it should versus sitting and clicking coupons for a large asset managers and not.
turns.zh: 我的第一个期望是：它能像本该的那样，出于慈善目的被真正投出去，而不是躺在那里替大型资产管理公司数着息票、无所作为。

turns.en: But my second hope is that at least while it's waiting to be put to work is that it's invested more aligned with an impact mission versus a non impact mission or oftentimes maybe invest in things that are counter to what that donor even wants to do philanthropically. But it has not happened yet. I mean, it's starting slowly.
turns.zh: 我的第二个期望是：至少在它等待被投出去的那段时间里，它的投资能更契合影响力使命，而不是与之无关，甚至常常投在一些和捐赠人慈善意愿完全相悖的东西上。但这件事至今还没发生，只能说正在缓慢起步。

turns.en: A lot of organizations are doing it and your position a lot of co-invest in secondaries. I'm curious to start off with co-invest. What is the process there? Is it only for the fund managers that you currently work with? Or is it an opportunity to meet net new relationships? Talk to me about how you all approach co-invest.
turns.zh: 很多机构已经在做了。你们也做了很多联合投资和二级市场投资。我想先从联合投资聊起：流程是怎样的？只面向你们目前合作的基金管理人吗？还是说这也是结识全新关系的机会？跟我讲讲你们是怎么做联合投资的。

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, when I say co-invest, it is talking about specifically investing alongside a manager that we're invested in. We do have a really robust approach of trying to build a network of deal flow partners more broadly that we shared deals with and investments with.
turns.zh: 嗯，我说联合投资时，特指和我们已经投过的管理人一起、在同一笔项目上并行投资。不过我们也有一套相当成熟的做法，去更广地搭建一个项目流伙伴网络，彼此分享项目和投资。

turns.en: That's an important part of our sourcing and diligence process. But yeah, I think for co-invest me for us, given we are a bit broader from a thematic standpoint, to be able to leverage as I was mentioning some of the expertise in the fund managers that were invested in and co-invest alongside them in a category where they have real depth of expertise is one piece.
turns.zh: 这是我们项目来源和尽调流程中很重要的一环。至于联合投资，对我们来说——考虑到我们在主题上铺得比较宽——能像我前面提到的那样，借助我们所投基金管理人的专业能力，在他们真正有深厚专长的品类里和他们一起投，这是第一层价值。

turns.en: The second is getting some later stage exposure. So as I mentioned, most of our investments are at the seed series A stage. But we do do about 25% 30% of our investments at the series B plus and or private equity stage.
turns.zh: 第二层是获得一些后期阶段的敞口。就像我提到的，我们大部分投资都在种子轮和 A 轮，但确实有大约 25% 到 30% 的投资落在 B 轮及以后，或者私募股权阶段。

turns.en: We think for our investors, which again are mostly individuals and families, it's a nice add to the portfolio that creates maybe near term liquidity or just some less risk in the portfolio.
turns.zh: 我们认为，对我们的投资人——他们主要还是个人和家族——来说，这是对组合很好的补充，可能带来较近的流动性，或者让整个组合的风险低一些。

turns.en: And so we've taken an approach of building a portfolio that has those early stage higher risk, higher return potential bets, but then adding in some later stage exposure.
turns.zh: 所以我们的做法是：搭一个组合，里面既有早期那些高风险、高潜在回报的下注，同时也加入一些后期阶段的敞口。

turns.en: And the fact that we can do that through our fund manager partners makes it doable, right? We couldn't be sourcing directly across all stages. So that's how we think about the co-invest piece.
turns.zh: 而我们能通过基金管理人伙伴做到这一点，这才让它变得可行，对吧？我们不可能在所有阶段都自己直接找项目。这就是我们对联合投资这块的思考。

turns.en: So where are some of the opportunities you see, half of your practice is investing in climate, the rest in social impact like education, health care, financial inclusion.
turns.zh: 那你看到的机会都在哪儿？你们的投资里有一半投在气候，另一半投在教育、医疗、普惠金融这类社会影响力领域。

turns.en: If you're suggesting what rocks we should be looking under for the next decade of venture returns, what opportunities are there? Are there any trends that sort of have unlocked for some of these areas?
turns.zh: 如果让你来指路，未来十年的风投回报我们该翻哪些石头，机会在哪儿？有没有哪些趋势已经把这些领域给解锁了？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, one of the exciting ones, which was more, historically I would describe it as some sort of a challenge is a lot of the companies that we invest in take like education and health care as two sectors.
turns.zh: 嗯，有一个令人兴奋的点——历史上我更愿意把它描述成一种挑战：我们投的很多公司，就拿教育和医疗这两个行业来说，

turns.en: If you're thinking about how do you improve an outcome or have an impact in those areas, oftentimes it's not just with software technology.
turns.zh: 如果你想的是怎么在这些领域改善结果、创造影响力，那很多时候靠的并不只是软件技术。

turns.en: Often you're required to have people, soft services, maybe even hardware involved. And so a lot of the companies that we invest in, most of the companies we invest in are not just pure software businesses.
turns.zh: 你往往还需要有人力、有软性服务，甚至可能还要涉及硬件。所以我们投的很多公司，其实是大多数公司，都不是纯软件生意。

turns.en: And that's historically been a challenge where they're maybe lower margin, kind of the scale abilities a little bit lower. And so it was harder for them to raise fall one capital or kind of tap into mainstream venture for some of those reasons.
turns.zh: 而这在历史上一直是个难题：它们的利润率可能更低，可扩展性也差一些，因此出于这些原因，它们更难融到后续轮次的钱，也更难接上主流风投。

turns.en: And AI has been a huge transformation for those businesses and those categories where they're able to embed AI into the core product, really improve margins, have much broader accessibility, still very focused on the quality outcomes, but really change the profile and the economics of these businesses.
turns.zh: 而 AI 给这些企业和这些品类带来了巨大的改变：它们可以把 AI 嵌进核心产品，真正提升利润率，让可及性大幅拓宽，同时依然紧紧盯着结果质量——但确实改变了这些生意的形态和经济模型。

turns.en: And so for our portfolio, it's been a huge benefit to just see growth that was going to be harder come a lot quicker to see the efficiency of the capital that they're raising and putting the work. And so I think that's going to create a great opportunity for some of these maybe harder to invest in categories historically.
turns.zh: 所以对我们的组合来说，这是巨大的利好：眼看着原本会更难实现的增长来得快了很多，也能看到他们募来的钱在使用上的效率。

turns.en: And I think other venture firms are seeing this and are investing more actively, but I think that's going to be a huge benefit for the categories that we invest in and just very optimistic view on some of these categories being improved in a way that was much harder before AI.
turns.zh: 我认为这会给那些历史上更难投的品类带来很好的机会。我也觉得其他风投机构正在看到这一点，并且在更积极地出手。但我认为，这对我们投的这些品类会是巨大的利好；对于其中一些品类能以 AI 出现之前难得多的方式被改造升级，我非常乐观。

turns.en: Well, we started this conversation about your community building and I wanted to end it with an invitation for folks to get involved or if they're interested in gratitude ventures. So if you're a family office or an emerging manager, how do I get in touch with your group?
turns.zh: 我们是从你们如何做社群建设聊起的，那我也想用一个邀请来收尾——如果有人想参与进来，或者对 Gratitude Ventures 感兴趣。所以，如果你是家族办公室，或者是新锐管理人，该怎么联系你们？

turns.en: We do have open queries on our website and we review those go right into our Slack channel, we review them on a weekly basis. So again, back to that access piece, it's always important to us that we're taking people that are interested.
turns.zh: 我们网站上有一个开放的咨询入口，那些信息会直接进到我们的 Slack 频道里，我们每周都会过一遍。所以还是回到“可及性”这一点：认真对待每一个有兴趣的人，对我们来说始终很重要。

turns.en: Our view is again, we want more entrepreneurs, more family offices investing in the impact investing space and mission driven businesses. So we're here to help and navigate whether it's our community or our investments is a second-order question, not the first question, it's kind of how can we help you navigate this space.
turns.zh: 我们的想法还是那句：我们希望有更多创业者、更多家族办公室来投影响力投资和使命驱动型企业。所以我们就是来帮忙引路的。至于最后是通过我们的社群还是我们的投资，那是第二顺位的问题，不是第一个问题——第一个问题是：我们能怎么帮你在这个领域里找到路。

turns.en: So reach out through our website, also happy to connect on LinkedIn or happy to share my email. We do a lot of events throughout the year, we do in-person events all throughout the country, we do virtual events and many of those events are kind of more open to the broad ecosystem.
turns.zh: 所以可以通过我们的网站联系我们，也欢迎在 LinkedIn 上加我，或者我直接把邮箱给你也行。我们一年会办很多活动，在全国各地办线下活动，也办线上活动，其中很多活动是更加向整个生态开放的。

turns.en: And so happy to find ways where we can actually invite people to connect into the community directly and meet other folks and not just connect with me and the team. Great. Thanks so much, Thomas. Thanks, Thomas. Thank you. You later, allocator. After portfolio tile, investing with a smile. Hey, listen.
turns.zh: 所以我很乐意想办法，让大家能真正被邀请进来、直接融入社群、认识其他人，而不只是和我和我的团队建立联系。太好了，非常感谢你，Thomas。谢谢你，Thomas。谢谢你们。回头见，allocator。走过组合的试炼，依然带着微笑做投资。嘿，听好了。
